Create a reference

Source: R/references.R
sf_reference.Rd

Builds one bibliographic reference as a CSL-JSON record, the format that Zotero, Mendeley and pandoc share. Attach references to an instrument with add_references() or through sf_instrument(components = ), cite them in text as [@id], and render_report() lists every cited reference once, at the end of the report.

Usage

sf_reference(
  id,
  title,
  author = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  type = "article-journal",
  container = NULL,
  volume = NULL,
  issue = NULL,
  pages = NULL,
  publisher = NULL,
  edition = NULL,
  editor = NULL,
  doi = NULL,
  url = NULL,
  version = NULL,
  language = NULL,
  cited_by = NULL
)

Arguments

id

Character. The citation key, for example "cohen_1988". Starts with a letter, digit or underscore, as pandoc requires.

title

Character. The work's title.

author

Character vector of names written "Family, Given", or a single organisation name written "{R Core Team}" in braces. NULL when the work has no named author.

year

Integer or character. Year of publication.

type

Character. A CSL item type: "article-journal" (default), "book", "chapter", "paper-conference", "report", "thesis", "webpage", "software", "dataset", "manuscript" or "document".

container

Character. The journal, or the book a chapter is in.

volume, issue, pages

Character. Volume, issue and page range, for example "591-611", or an article number.

publisher

Character. Publisher, or for a thesis the institution.

edition

Character. Edition, for example "2".

editor

Character vector of editor names, written as for author.

doi

Character. The bare DOI, leaving off the https://doi.org/ prefix.

url

Character. A web address.

version

Character. A software version.

language

Character. The work's language as a code, for example "fr". Set it for a work in another language: a citation style title-cases English titles only, and would otherwise capitalise "et" or "ir" in a French or Lithuanian journal name.

cited_by

Character vector. Where the instrument cites this reference: "instrument", "item:<id>", "scale:<id>", "plan:<block id>" or "model:<id>". Optional.

Value

An object of class sf_reference.

See also

read_bibtex(), add_references(), sframe_references()

Examples

ref <- sf_reference(
  id = "cronbach_1951", type = "article-journal",
  author = "Cronbach, L. J.", year = 1951,
  title = "Coefficient alpha and the internal structure of tests",
  container = "Psychometrika", volume = "16", issue = "3",
  pages = "297-334", cited_by = "scale:satisfaction"
)
ref$id
#> [1] "cronbach_1951"
